k: Halt! By order of the Lord-Commander, every traveler on this causeway is to be searched for—
src: 'Halt! By order of the Lord-Commander, every traveler on this causeway is to be searched for—'

k: Black hair. Pale. That's _her_. That's the—
src: 'Black hair. Pale. That\'s _her_. That\'s the—'

k: Sergeant! Is it Sergeant? I can't tell with the helmet. Hello. We are a traveling theater troupe.
src: 'Sergeant! Is it Sergeant? I can\'t tell with the helmet. Hello. We are a traveling theater troupe.'

k: Kestrel? Bram _Kestrel_?
src: 'Kestrel? Bram _Kestrel_?'

k: Not a very _good_ theater troupe.
src: 'Not a very _good_ theater troupe.'

k: Take the girl! The rest are worth nothing!
src: 'Take the girl! The rest are worth nothing!'

k: The Lord-Commander will hear of this, Kestrel! He'll — he'll—
src: 'The Lord-Commander will hear of this, Kestrel! He\'ll — he\'ll—'

k: They knew my name.
src: 'They knew my name.'

k: Everybody knows your name, big man. You say it very loudly.
src: 'Everybody knows your name, big man. You say it very loudly.'

k: Garrick has pickets this far south. Either he's ahead of us, or he's everywhere.
src: 'Garrick has pickets this far south. Either he\'s ahead of us, or he\'s everywhere.'

k: Then we keep moving.
src: 'Then we keep moving.'

k: Word came down the water: Mother Osk's sitting up and shouting at people. Best news I've had in a month.
src: 'Word came down the water: Mother Osk\'s sitting up and shouting at people. Best news I\'ve had in a month.'

k: If you're ever back this way, my punt's yours. Free. Well. Half price.
src: 'If you\'re ever back this way, my punt\'s yours. Free. Well. Half price.'

k: Gaspar's the name, poling's the game. Was the game. Nobody's crossing the fen since the light went out.
src: 'Gaspar\'s the name, poling\'s the game. Was the game. Nobody\'s crossing the fen since the light went out.'

k: Mother Osk took the fever the very night the Choir barge came. Coincidence, the Choir said. Very sure of themselves, the Choir.
src: 'Mother Osk took the fever the very night the Choir barge came. Coincidence, the Choir said. Very sure of themselves, the Choir.'

k: The village is east. Mind the toads. They've gone strange.
src: 'The village is east. Mind the toads. They\'ve gone strange.'

k: Are you from the Cathedral? Did they send it back? Did they—
src: 'Are you from the Cathedral? Did they send it back? Did they—'

k: Oh. You're... you're children.
src: 'Oh. You\'re... you\'re children.'

k: We're carrying letters to the Keepers. From Aurenne. The Hierophant sent us.
src: 'We\'re carrying letters to the Keepers. From Aurenne. The Hierophant sent us.'

k: _The Hierophant._
src: '_The Hierophant._'

k: Then you're too late. Or too early. I don't know which.
src: 'Then you\'re too late. Or too early. I don\'t know which.'

k: Mother Osk has the rot. The black-vein fever. Doctor Vey says she won't see morning.
src: 'Mother Osk has the rot. The black-vein fever. Doctor Vey says she won\'t see morning.'

k: Where is she?
src: 'Where is she?'

k: In the Lantern. She won't let us move her. She says a Keeper dies at her light.
src: 'In the Lantern. She won\'t let us move her. She says a Keeper dies at her light.'

k: ...Even when the light's gone out.
src: '...Even when the light\'s gone out.'

k: I'm a Mender. Take me to her. Now, please.
src: 'I\'m a Mender. Take me to her. Now, please.'

k: The Lantern — north-east, past the Rot House! Hurry!
src: 'The Lantern — north-east, past the Rot House! Hurry!'

k: Well. That's the soup off.
src: 'Well. That\'s the soup off.'

k: I know. I know. Jokes are a reflex. Like flinching.
src: 'I know. I know. Jokes are a reflex. Like flinching.'

k: Mirefen. Mother Osk is dying of the Gloam-rot, and her Lantern is dark. Ilse didn't even wait to be asked.
src: 'Mirefen. Mother Osk is dying of the Gloam-rot, and her Lantern is dark. Ilse didn\'t even wait to be asked.'

k: The room smells of willow bark and fever. In the bed against the wall, under three blankets, a small old woman is shivering hard enough to rattle the frame.
src: 'The room smells of willow bark and fever. In the bed against the wall, under three blankets, a small old woman is shivering hard enough to rattle the frame.'

k: ...told him no. Told him no, told him _no_—
src: '...told him no. Told him no, told him _no_—'

k: She's been saying that for two days.
src: 'She\'s been saying that for two days.'

k: ...Ysolde?
src: '...Ysolde?'

k: Ysolde Halloway, you've got _old_. Where are your manners? Where's my tea?
src: 'Ysolde Halloway, you\'ve got _old_. Where are your manners? Where\'s my tea?'

k: That's my mother.
src: 'That\'s my mother.'

k: Course it is. Same chin. Stubborn chin. I told your mother no too, didn't I. No, no—
src: 'Course it is. Same chin. Stubborn chin. I told your mother no too, didn\'t I. No, no—'

k: Black veins to the shoulder. Fever — very high. And her breath—
src: 'Black veins to the shoulder. Fever — very high. And her breath—'

k: It rattles. It's in her lungs.
src: 'It rattles. It\'s in her lungs.'

k: Three weeks of rot, four days of fever. It's at her shoulder now. I've tried willow, feverfew, eel-oil and prayer. In that order, then in every other order.
src: 'Three weeks of rot, four days of fever. It\'s at her shoulder now. I\'ve tried willow, feverfew, eel-oil and prayer. In that order, then in every other order.'

k: You're the Mender? You're _sixteen_.
src: 'You\'re the Mender? You\'re _sixteen_.'

k: And you're out of ideas.
src: 'And you\'re out of ideas.'

k: ...Sorry. That was — I'm sorry.
src: '...Sorry. That was — I\'m sorry.'

k: Don't be. It's true.
src: 'Don\'t be. It\'s true.'

k: My grandmother has a book. There's a recipe in it — _for the black-vein fever of the fens._
src: 'My grandmother has a book. There\'s a recipe in it — _for the black-vein fever of the fens._'

k: Lanternmoss, for the light it remembers. A weepcap lily, for the dark it grew in. And the gall of the thing that's making it.
src: 'Lanternmoss, for the light it remembers. A weepcap lily, for the dark it grew in. And the gall of the thing that\'s making it.'

k: The old bog remedy. Every grandmother in Mirefen knows it.
src: 'The old bog remedy. Every grandmother in Mirefen knows it.'

k: Every grandmother in Mirefen also knows that lanternmoss only grows on the Sunken Shrine, weepcaps only in the Root Grotto, and whatever's making the rot lives in the black pool at the heart of the Drownmere.
src: 'Every grandmother in Mirefen also knows that lanternmoss only grows on the Sunken Shrine, weepcaps only in the Root Grotto, and whatever\'s making the rot lives in the black pool at the heart of the Drownmere.'

k: Nobody has come back out of the Drownmere since the Lantern went dark.
src: 'Nobody has come back out of the Drownmere since the Lantern went dark.'

k: Nobody has gone in with a Vanguard, a Warden, a — whatever Sable is—
src: 'Nobody has gone in with a Vanguard, a Warden, a — whatever Sable is—'

k: —a thief and a pirate.
src: '—a thief and a pirate.'

k: Rogue. It's a Crest now. I'm _official_.
src: 'Rogue. It\'s a Crest now. I\'m _official_.'

k: Three things. One: Doctor Vey keeps her breathing until we're back. Two: I'll need a mortar and a clean pot. Three—
src: 'Three things. One: Doctor Vey keeps her breathing until we\'re back. Two: I\'ll need a mortar and a clean pot. Three—'

k: Three: we're going into the bog.
src: 'Three: we\'re going into the bog.'

k: Three: _I'm_ going into the bog. You're coming because you'd follow me anyway.
src: 'Three: _I\'m_ going into the bog. You\'re coming because you\'d follow me anyway.'

k: _(grinning)_ Same as always?
src: '_(grinning)_ Same as always?'

k: Opposite of always.
src: 'Opposite of always.'

k: Take the punt from the south jetty. I'll tell the warden to let you through.
src: 'Take the punt from the south jetty. I\'ll tell the warden to let you through.'

k: ...Thank you. You don't even know her.
src: '...Thank you. You don\'t even know her.'

k: I know what a fever is.
src: 'I know what a fever is.'

k: Ilse has a plan. Ilse always has a plan — but this one is HERS, and I'm following it into a bog. I think she's been waiting her whole life for someone to need her this much.
src: 'Ilse has a plan. Ilse always has a plan — but this one is HERS, and I\'m following it into a bog. I think she\'s been waiting her whole life for someone to need her this much.'

k: Mother Osk is asleep, or something like it. Her lips keep moving.
src: 'Mother Osk is asleep, or something like it. Her lips keep moving.'

k: _No. No. No._
src: '_No. No. No._'

k: Still here? Elowen's in the Heartwood, past Rootholm, through the Thornwood. North out of the village, then east.
src: 'Still here? Elowen\'s in the Heartwood, past Rootholm, through the Thornwood. North out of the village, then east.'

k: Tell her Osk says she still owes me a goose. She'll know.
src: 'Tell her Osk says she still owes me a goose. She\'ll know.'

k: Ysolde's girl. Go on, then. Go and be stubborn somewhere useful.
src: 'Ysolde\'s girl. Go on, then. Go and be stubborn somewhere useful.'

k: And if you see your mother before I do — tell her I said she was right. She'll hate that.
src: 'And if you see your mother before I do — tell her I said she was right. She\'ll hate that.'

k: You did it? You really — go on, go to her! Quickly!
src: 'You did it? You really — go on, go to her! Quickly!'

k: The Drownmere's past the south jetty. Bring the punt back. Bring yourselves back.
src: 'The Drownmere\'s past the south jetty. Bring the punt back. Bring yourselves back.'

k: I keep making her soup. She can't eat it. I keep making it.
src: 'I keep making her soup. She can\'t eat it. I keep making it.'

k: Please. Whatever you can do.
src: 'Please. Whatever you can do.'

k: I polish the cradle every morning. For when the stone comes back.
src: 'I polish the cradle every morning. For when the stone comes back.'

k: It will come back. Won't it?
src: 'It will come back. Won\'t it?'

k: I gave it to them, you know. The stone.
src: 'I gave it to them, you know. The stone.'

k: I stood there and let them carry it out of the Lantern, because they had a seal and I had a fever and a frightened face.
src: 'I stood there and let them carry it out of the Lantern, because they had a seal and I had a fever and a frightened face.'

k: Mother Osk says it isn't my fault.
src: 'Mother Osk says it isn\'t my fault.'

k: ...She's right.
src: '...She\'s right.'

k: Is she? Then how do you stop feeling like it is?
src: 'Is she? Then how do you stop feeling like it is?'

k: I don't know. I'll tell you if I find out.
src: 'I don\'t know. I\'ll tell you if I find out.'

k: Here. Lamp-oil from the Lantern. The last of it. It burns blue, and the Gloam hates it.
src: 'Here. Lamp-oil from the Lantern. The last of it. It burns blue, and the Gloam hates it.'

k: Welcome to the Leaning Heron! It leans. The beer doesn't. Sixty gold a bed, and tonight the beds are full of the _living_. Cheers to the Mender!
src: 'Welcome to the Leaning Heron! It leans. The beer doesn\'t. Sixty gold a bed, and tonight the beds are full of the _living_. Cheers to the Mender!'

k: Welcome to the Leaning Heron. It leans. The beer doesn't. Half my rooms are full of folk waiting to die, half are full of folk waiting to bury them. Sixty gold and I'll find you a third half.
src: 'Welcome to the Leaning Heron. It leans. The beer doesn\'t. Half my rooms are full of folk waiting to die, half are full of folk waiting to bury them. Sixty gold and I\'ll find you a third half.'

k: the Leaning Heron
src: 'the Leaning Heron'

k: _Seven lights at the edge of the world, / seven Keepers keeping; / one by the sea and one in the sand, / one where the snow lies sleeping;_
src: '_Seven lights at the edge of the world, / seven Keepers keeping; / one by the sea and one in the sand, / one where the snow lies sleeping;_'
